about.label: SIFMUN/ABOUT
about.title: A forum that speaks three languages.
about.p1: SIFMUN is the Strategic International Forum Model United Nations, based in Fergana, Uzbekistan. For one day, students become delegates. Each one takes a country, learns its position, and defends it in committee.
about.p2: Every session runs in English, Uzbek and Russian, so you can speak in the language you think in.
about.photoAlt: Organiser, chair and delegate badges held together in a circle

mun.title: One day as a diplomat.
mun.lede: Model United Nations is a game played in earnest. For one day you stop being a student and become a delegate: you speak for a country, in a UN body, on a problem the real world has not solved yet.
mun.s1p: Before the conference you receive a country and a committee. Often it is not your own country. You read its history, its allies and its red lines, until you can answer for it.
mun.s2p: The chair calls the countries one by one. You raise your placard and answer: present. From this moment nobody in the room calls you by your name, only by your country.
mun.s3p: Your first speech: about a minute to tell the room where your country stands. The gavel falls when your time runs out, so every word has to count.
mun.s4p: Then the room comes alive. In a moderated caucus the chair gives the floor speech by speech. In an unmoderated caucus you leave your seat, find allies, argue in whispers and trade a clause for a vote.
mun.s5p: Allies write a draft resolution together: what the world should do, clause by clause. Others amend it, attack it and defend it, line by line.
mun.s6p: Placards go up: for, against, abstain. The resolution passes or falls, and you feel what diplomacy really costs.
mun.s7p: At the closing ceremony the chairs name the strongest delegates of each committee. Every participant leaves with a certificate, and with a new way of speaking.
mun.note: You do not need experience. You need to prepare, to listen and to take the floor.
